intro.title: Position: fixed and sticky
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage with a navigation bar that stays fixed at the top of the screen and a section that sticks to the top as you scroll. You will learn how to use the CSS `position` property with the values `fixed` and `sticky` to control element placement relative to the viewport. The main technologies involved are CSS selectors and the `position`, `top`, and `z-index` properties. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you create interactive, scroll-aware layouts commonly seen in modern websites.
intro.usecase: Fixed and sticky positioning are essential for creating persistent UI elements that remain visible during user interaction. You'll use position: fixed for navigation bars that stay at the top of the screen while scrolling, cookie consent banners that remain at the bottom, and chat widgets that stay in the corner. Position: sticky is perfect for table headers that remain visible as you scroll through data tables, section headings in long documentation pages, and filter panels in e-commerce product listings. These techniques are fundamental for improving usability in dashboards, forms, and any application requiring persistent access to key controls.
